sights.address: 7 Lorong Buangkok (off Gerald Drive, via Buangkok Crescent), Singapore 547557
sights.w: Singapore's last surviving mainland village, established in 1956 when traditional-medicine seller Sng Teow Koon bought the swampy land and rented plots to Malay and Chinese families. A cluster of zinc-roofed houses on dirt tracks around a surau, in the Trafalgar (Buangkok) subzone of Hougang; Ms Sng Mui Hong, the founder's youngest daughter, still lives here as landlord. Old four-digit street signs survive.
sights.k: Free; a living village — visit respectfully, don't enter homes

sights.address: Lorong Halus Wetland, Lorong Halus North (eastern bank of Serangoon Reservoir), Singapore
sights.w: An 18-football-field wetland on the Hougang/Defu edge — a former landfill transformed into a natural water-treatment site whose cattails bio-remediate rainwater before it enters the adjoining Serangoon Reservoir. Bounded by Kangkar to the west and Defu Industrial Park to the south, it's a family recreation spot reached over the red steel-railway-style Lorong Halus Bridge from Punggol Promenade.
sights.k: Open daily, free; cycling, fishing decks & birdwatching

sights.w: One of Singapore's first Chinese mission schools, founded in 1892 as Tao Nan School in the Upper Serangoon village and renamed Holy Innocents' Chinese Boys' School in 1920 under Fr Becheras. Part of Hougang's 'Holy Land' cluster of Catholic institutions around the Church of the Nativity; the school returned to a rebuilt Hougang campus, blessed by Archbishop Nicholas Chia in 2006.
sights.k: Active school; grounds not open to visitors

sights.w: A Taoist temple complex completed in 1996 and a Hougang Heritage Trail 'Architectural Gems' landmark. It houses three older temples — Kai Hock Tong, Keat Sun Beo and Chao Ying Kong — relocated and consolidated from their original sites at Wolskel Road, Lorong Chuan and Yishun, a common Singapore story of temples resettled by redevelopment.

sights.address: Foot of Sungei Serangoon near Upper Serangoon Road (former 7½ milestone), Hougang, Singapore
sights.w: The historic Teochew settlement of Kangkar — 'foot of the river' — at the mouth of Sungei Serangoon, once home to the bustling Kangkar fish market at the 7½ milestone. Its 60-year fishing trade ceased in the 1980s when the fishermen and merchants were relocated to the new Punggol Fishing Port to make way for Hougang New Town; a Hougang Heritage Trail stop.
sights.k: Interpretive heritage site along the trail
